Felahiye Ilcesi, Kepic Koyu sinirlari icinde yer almaktadir. Soz konusu yapinin
Gec Roma Cagi'na ait bir mezar aniti oldugu bilinmektedirlo (Resim: 9). Bu yapinin
yaninda dogal kaya uzerinde, Roma Cag1'na ait bir hoyuk yer almaktadir. Yapi, gecmisten
gunumuze degin define arayanlarin ve eski eser kacakcilarinin hedefi olmus ve bu
nedenle pek cok tahribata ugramistir (Resim: 10). Yapinin bir bolumu cokmus; tonoz
ust ortusu ile arka cephesindeki alinlik penceresi yikilmistir. Yapinin icindeki ayaklarca
tasinan kemer sayesinde, tonozun yikilmasi belli bir noktada, kemer hizasinda durmustur.
Fakat tonozun cokusu sirasinda, kemerde de statik sorunlar olusmus, cokmeler baslamis;
kemer tonozdan ayrilmis ve asagiya dogru sarkmistir (Resim: 11). Kemerin kilit tas1 da
dahil olmak uzere ortasindaki uc kemer blogu parcalanmis ve yerinden kaymistir. Bu
bloklarin herhangi bir sarsintt ya da zaman icindeki bozulmalari sonucunda, yerlerinden
asagiya dusmeleri neticesinde, oncelikle kemer tamamen cokecek, ardindan yapinin
tonozundaki yikilma devam edecek ve yapidaki tahribat buyuk olcude artacaktir. Mevcut
durumu ile kemerdeki bozulmalar, yapida ciddi bir cokme tehlikesi yaratmaktadir. Bu
sekli ile yapinin icine girilmesi can guvenligini de tehdit etmektedir. Bu tehlikenin yani
sira, yapiya mudahale edilmemesi durumunda meydana gelecek olasi bir cokme, yapinin
yikim surecini baslatacag1 gibi, bu cokmenin ardindan yapilacak restorasyon da daha
zor ve maliyetli olacaktir. Ayrica boyle bir yikim sonucu yapinin ozgunlugu bozulacak
olmasindan dolay1 yapi telafisi mumkun olmayan buyuk bir zarara ugramis olacaktir.
Butun bu sebeplerden oturu, bolge icin essiz olan ve insan eliyle yapilan tum tahribatlara
ragmen halen ayakta duran bu anitsal yapiya acil olarak mudahale edilmesi ve gerekli
koruma onlemlerinin alinmas1 gerekmektedir.

Bu bakimdan uzerinde dikkatle durulmasi gereken husus, rabi sikkitim sifatindaki yuksek

Wahsusana'nin kiralinin Purushattum buyuk kirallig1 cevresinde ona bagli diger kirallik-

Der Adressat des Hauptbriefes, Himuili, war nach den Briefen von.
Masat ein bel mudgalti, "Militar- bzw. Grenzgouverneur". In der Korre-.
spondenz von Masat steht er unter den Beamten, die vom GroBkonig
Briefe erhalten, nach Kassu an zweiter Stelle. Letzterer trug den Titel uGU-
LA NimGiR.eRinMes "Anfuhrer der Truppeninspektoren". Beide Funktionare
mussen ihre Amter zur selben Zeit in Masat ausgeubt haben. Eine Unter-
scheidung der militarischen Befugnisse der beiden Generale war mir bisher
nicht moglich. Das Amt des be! madgalti beinhaltete neben militarischen
aber auch zivile, gerichtliche und verwaltungsmaBige Funktionen. Darunter
spielte die Kontrolle uber das Lehnswesen eine wichtige Rolle. Die Infor-
mationen, die wir aus den Masat-Texten gewinnen, stehen in Einklang mit
unsereren Kenntnissen aus den Bogazkoy-Texten und insbesondere aus den
bel-madgalti-Instruktionen, deren Bearbeitung wir zum groBten Teil dem
verehrten Jubilar verdanken: E. von Schuler, Hethitische Dienstanweisun-
gen (AfO Bh. 1O) 36ff.
Der Nachtragsbrief stammt von Tarhunmiya (gelegentlich auch mDIM-
miya oder mDu-miya geschrieben), welcher in den Masat-Briefen der am
besten bekannte Schreiber aus der Kanzlei von Hattusa ist. Der Nachtrags-
brief ist ebenfalls an Himuili gerichtet. Er behandelt z.T. dasselbe Thema
in einem achtungsvollen, personlichen und privaten Ton. Sein Anliegen.
betreffs seines Hauses in Masat beschaftigt Tarhunmiya auch in seinen
anderen Nachtragsbriefen..
Unser Brief ist auch deshalb von Interesse, weil er in bezug auf.
Sahhan und luzzi eine enge Parallele zu einem in Meskene/Emar in Syrien
gefundenen Brief liefert. Darauf werde ich weiter unten zurickkommen..
Auf diese Parallele hat auch Fiorella Imparati in einem in Ankara im
Fruhjahr 1988 gehaltenen Vortrag hingewiesen. Der Inhalt unserer Masat-
Tafel war ihr aus einem Vortrag bekannt, den ich im Jahre 1984 in Flo-
renz gehalten hatte..

According to the records of the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations in Ankara, more than
1600 tablets were unearthed during the excavations at Kultepe in 1950.4 T. Ozguc states in
his related report that the tablets of that year came from various trenches.5 Upon their
discovery some of the documents were entirely and some partly published by a number of
researchers in different periodicals, particularly by K. Balkan.
The fact that the place names Balihum and Luhuzattiya in the two new texts under dis-
cussion and in one previously published document were recorded together suggests one of
two possibilities. The less likely of the two is that Balihum and Luhuzattiya were neigh-
bouring centres. This possibility, however, can be considered unlikely in view of the
existence of a river and related settlement centre known as Balihum located far from the
stations immediately preceding Kanis, where Luhuzattiya should be sought.6 The second,
and the stronger, possibility is thus that the two centres were recorded together due to
them both being cities well known for their wool and wool products. Although these docu-
ments include no information relevant to the localization of Balihum and Luhuzattiya,
they enable one to suggest that these two cities known for their wools were centres where
caprid husbandry played a particularly important role. As is well known, a considerable
number of the Kultepe tablets are concerned with wool commerce'. Balihum and Luhuzat-
tiya are mentioned in both of the new documents in the context of instructions to give an
unknown amount of wool (saptum/sig) to Ennanum, the son of Abiya.
